question: Which Session of Congress and Muslim League reached an understanding of creating a joint front against the British regime?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lucknow Pact** was signed between the **Indian National Congress** and the **All India Muslim League** in **December 1916.**
 
• The pact aimed at creating a united front against British colonialism in India and to secure greater **self-governance** for Indians.
 
• The agreement was significant because it marked the first time the **Congress and the Muslim League** had come to a compromise on the issue of self-government.
 
• The pact also led to the formation of the **League-Congress joint committee,** which worked towards the goal of Indian independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian National Congress **was founded in** Bombay in 1885**.

 
 
• It was founded by **Allan Octavian Hume.**
 
• However, there was** no joint front** between the Congress and the Muslim League at this time.
 
 
 
• The** Allahabad Address** was given by **Allama Iqbal in 1930,** where he proposed the idea of a separate **Muslim state **in India, which later became **Pakistan.**
 
• The **Delhi Durbar of 1911 **was a grand imperial gathering held in Delhi to celebrate the coronation of **King George V as Emperor of India.**
